logline: 규방 반짇고리의 일곱 벗이 바느질 공을 다투다 부인의 꾸지람에 화해한다
anchor: a Korean boy of about ten in hemp clothes, his small sister beside him
palette: silk cream, deep cinnabar red, lacquer black, warm lamplight gold, celadon green

beats.beat: 깊은 밤 규방 반짇고리의 일곱 벗
beats.visual: the quiet inner room by night, lamplight low and gold: the open round sewing basket sits open on the lacquered table, and in and around it the seven companions of the needlework rest in their places — a folded bamboo measure, black iron scissors, a bright silver needle on a pincushion, spools of blue red black and white silk, a brass-headed indu, a round charcoal iron on its stand, and one small worn leather thimble half hidden at the basket's rim; the mistress's cushion lies empty, the peony screen stands in shadow, and the whole composition is a chaekgeori still-life holding its breath, as if the seven might begin to speak the moment the lamp flame steadies
beats.motion: the lamp flame sways once and steadies, its gold light sliding slowly across bamboo, iron, silver, silk, brass and worn leather in turn, each of the seven glinting awake as the light finds it; a thread-end curls off the red spool and settles, the peony screen breathes shadow, and the camera drifts in slowly over the rim of the red-silk basket

beats.visual: a tight tabletop close-up with room for nothing but the work: two pale hands hold the folded bamboo measure flat along the edge of undyed silk — the pale bamboo strip clearly ruled with fine black graduations, brass hinge pins bright — while a stub of tailor's chalk in the right hand draws a long straight line against the measure's edge; the chalk line runs away crisp and white across the weave, the red-silk basket rim glows soft at the frame's top corner, and lamplight lies warm along the bamboo — the measure's work shown in the doing, nothing else in frame but hands, silk, chalk and rule
beats.motion: the chalk stub travels the measure's edge in one slow steady draw, the white line lengthening perfectly straight behind it, the left hand's fingers pinning the bamboo flat so the brass pins press tiny dimples into the silk; chalk dust sifts fine off the line's end, lamplight gliding along the graduations as the draw completes, and the camera tracks with the chalk down the lengthening line

beats.visual: the black iron scissors take the stage on the part-cut silk, blades open in a wide graceful X, red-silk ring handles raised, the lamplight running a bright line down each curved edge; under the blades the silk shows one long clean cut, its two edges parted like water behind a boat — the scissors' evidence; the bamboo measure now leans back among the others at the basket, and the pincushion with its silver needle waits small at the table's edge; the open blades throw a scissor-shaped shadow across the peony screen, twice their size and twice as proud
beats.motion: the open blades ease wider and pivot slowly on one ring handle, turning the bright X of themselves slowly to every side of the room, lamplight sliding along the curved edges as they turn; the cut silk's two edges stir faintly in the moved air, the giant scissor-shadow wheels across the peony screen, and the camera circles the standing blades low along the tabletop

beats.visual: a fingertip close-up of the finest work: one pale hand steadies a fold of silk while the other guides the slender silver needle down through the weave mid-stitch, a scarlet strand running from the needle's threading hole in a taut bright arc; behind the moving needle stretches a row of stitches so small and even they read as faint dashes; the worn leather thimble sits capped on the middle finger of the guiding hand — old friend at its post — and everything beyond hands, silk, needle and thread falls to warm blurred lamplight
beats.motion: the needle dips and rises through the silk in one slow complete stitch, the scarlet strand drawing down and pulling gently taut as the loop closes into line with its tiny even row, the thimble-capped finger pushing the needle's head with a small precise press; the taut thread gleams as it settles, and the camera closes on the stitch tightening flush with the weave

beats.visual: the spools answer with color: threads of blue, red, black and white silk spill from their wooden spools in long smooth ribbons, curling across the plain pale silk and circling the upright silver needle in a loose bright ring; the scarlet strand through the needle's threading hole is plainly one of their own, and the four ribbons catch the lamp in glossy runs of pure color against the muted room; the other companions hold still at the basket, and the peony screen's blossoms look faded beside the threads' living dye
beats.motion: the four ribbons of thread uncurl further in slow simultaneous sweeps, each spool giving a lazy quarter-turn as its color pays out, the bright ring around the needle drawing gently closer; the scarlet strand in the threading hole lifts and sways, lamplight running along each glossy line, and the camera drifts above the ring of color looking straight down

beats.visual: the brass-headed indu rests on its small stone stand beside a folded seam: a little leaf-shaped head of polished brass on a long straight handle of dark wood, a faint heat-shimmer rising off the metal and trembling the lamp flame seen through it; where it has already passed, the silk seam lies pressed flat and quietly shining, and beside that finished seam a second seam still puckers and rolls, waiting its turn — the indu's evidence in before and after; the warm brass glows deeper gold than the lamp itself
beats.motion: the indu lifts its brass head from the stand in one slow steady rise and glides along the puckered seam, the cloth relaxing flat behind its passage in a spreading ribbon of sheen, heat-shimmer trembling above the moving metal; it reaches the seam's end and settles back onto its stone stand, the new-pressed silk gleaming, and the camera follows low along the flattening seam

beats.visual: a tight close-up over the ironing: two pale hands grip the long straight wooden handle of the charcoal iron — a shallow round brass pan, embers glowing dull red through its seams, one thin curl of smoke rising — and press it flat against a wide panel of red silk; behind the brass pan's round footprint the silk lies smooth and softly shining in a widening path, while ahead of it the cloth still rolls in low rumpled folds; the silk fills the whole frame edge to edge, whole and unmarked, and the ember-light warms the hands and the brass from below
beats.motion: the two hands drive the iron in one long slow pass across the silk, low folds smoothing flat and shining behind the gliding pan, embers brightening with the motion and the thin smoke-curl leaning back; the pressed path widens smooth and unbroken as the pass runs on, and the camera tracks low beside the advancing edge of sheen

beats.visual: the smallest of the seven has the humblest stage: the old leather thimble sits alone in the lamplight on the basket's red-silk rim, dome worn shiny and dark as an old servant's hands, its crown crossed with decades of tiny stitch-scars, each scar a needle-thrust it took so a fingertip would go unhurt; around it the grander six glint from the shadows — bamboo, iron, silver, silk, brass — but the light holds on the small dark dome, and beside it lies a single silver needle as if resting against an old friend; the room beyond is soft darkness and the peony screen leans close like someone listening
beats.motion: the old thimble tips forward in a slow small bow and rolls half a turn along the red-silk rim, its stitch-scarred crown passing through the lamplight so every old scar shows in turn, then rocks gently upright again beside the resting needle; the light seems to warm on the worn dome, the six grander companions hold their glints in the shadow, and the camera closes slowly on the little bowed veteran

beats.visual: the room turns: the gentlewoman is awake on her cushion, risen to one arm, jade jeogori catching the lamp, silver binyeo gleaming in her low chignon, and her calm dark eyes fixed on the sewing table with a long level look; before her the seven lie suddenly ordinary — measure folded, scissors closed, needle in the cushion, threads loose, indu and iron on their rests, thimble at the rim — the whole table gone quiet at her waking; her sleeve's long line points down the length of the table, and the lamp flame stands up straight in the stilled air
beats.motion: the gentlewoman rises from her cushion in one unhurried motion and settles before the table, her sleeve sweeping a slow arc that stills the whole room, her level gaze traveling from the folded measure down the line of seven to the small thimble at the rim; the lamp flame straightens, a loose thread-end settles as if swallowed, and the camera holds just over her shoulder looking down the length of the judged table

beats.visual: a close mournful still-life of only three wounds in the lamplight: at center the slender silver needle lying on red silk, bent slightly along its thin length; beside it a single pair of black iron scissors — the only scissors in the picture — open just enough to show one nicked edge and a loosened pivot screw; and before them the old leather thimble, stitch-scarred crown turned up; the three lie close together on the red silk, everything else — basket, screen, lamp — sunk into soft warm darkness around the three tired veterans
beats.motion: the lamplight breathes slowly over the three in turn — sliding along the needle's slight bend, glinting on the scissors' nicked edge, warming the thimble's scarred crown — while the red silk under them stirs by a thread's width as if the table itself sighed; nothing else moves in the soft darkness, and the camera drifts very slowly across the three held-up hurts

beats.visual: the judgment darkens: the gentlewoman kneels tall over the table with a plain wrapping cloth spread open beside the seven, her jade sleeve drawn back from one pale hand, the bojagi's wide square waiting flat and plain; the lamp gutters lower so the room's warm gold cools toward grey, the peony screen recedes into shadow, and the seven lie very still and very small between the spread cloth and her level eyes — the basket's red silk, an arm away, suddenly the far side of a river; her chignon's silver pin glints once, cold, and every thread-end in the room hangs motionless
beats.motion: her pale hand draws the wrapping cloth's near corner slowly across the table toward the seven, the plain fabric advancing slowly over the lacquer, its shadow arriving before it; the lamp gutters and the gold light cools, the seven seeming to shrink together as the corner nears, and the camera watches from table height, low behind the huddled tools, as the cloth comes on

beats.visual: at the tide's edge the smallest steps forward: the old leather thimble rolls out alone from the huddled seven, out across the lacquer to a spot before the gentlewoman's pale hand, and there tips itself over into a deep bow, scarred dome touching the table in a deep bow; the wrapping cloth's corner pauses at its shadow; above, the gentlewoman's level eyes rest on the little bowed dome and on the decades of stitch-scars offered up in the guttering light, and something at the corner of her composed mouth loosens; behind, the six hold their breath in a half-circle, and the lamp flame slowly warms again by one shade of gold
beats.motion: the thimble rolls forward in one small brave line and tips into its bow, scarred crown pressing the lacquer, holding perfectly still in the pause that follows; the cloth's advancing corner stops, the gentlewoman's hand settles slowly back to her knee, and the lamplight breathes one shade warmer over the little bowed dome while the camera closes on the space between the small penitent and the softening hand

beats.visual: warm gold restored: the gentlewoman sits at the table with the old thimble seated upright on her fingertip, her other hand smoothing the wrapping cloth folded harmlessly away, her composed face eased into the ghost of a smile; around the basket the six stand restored to their places — measure folded neat, scissors closed, needle upright in its cushion trailing scarlet, spools wound, indu and iron on their rests — all seven forgiven and returned to their places; the lamp burns tall, the peony screen's blossoms have their color back, and on the raised fingertip the little veteran's stitch-scars shine in the tall lamplight
beats.motion: her fingertip rises slowly with the thimble seated upon it, turning it gently in the tall lamplight so the old stitch-scars catch the light one by one; her other hand smooths the folded cloth flat and sets it aside, the six companions glinting easier in their places, and the camera rises with the crowned fingertip into the warm gold

beats.visual: morning light through the papered window, clear and pale gold: the sewing basket stands open on the lacquered table with all seven companions home and gleaming — measure folded, scissors nested, needle in the pincushion with its scarlet thread wound neat, spools in a color row, indu and charcoal iron cool on their rests, and the old thimble seated in the place of honor at the basket's center on the red silk; beside the basket lies a finished jeogori, seams flat, stitches invisible, collar crisp — the quiet work of seven quarrelsome friends and one patient hand; dust motes turn in the window light and the peony screen blooms mildly in the morning
beats.motion: only morning moves: dust motes turning in the pale gold window light, the scarlet thread-end stirring once against the pincushion, light creeping slowly across the finished jeogori's flat seams and up the basket's red silk to find the old thimble at its center; the room holds its clean stillness, and the camera pulls back slowly until basket, garment and morning window compose themselves into a chaekgeori still-life
